summary: POC scoping focused on security and compliance requirements for a pilot of Redwood's inference platform at Rivermark Health. Discussed SOC 2/ISO attestation, SSO/SAML via Okta, RBAC needs, audit logs and retention, KMS/HSM encryption, and network/VPC options. Scoped workload sizing and benchmark goals (95th perc latency <200ms for short completions, throughput ~50 rps), pilot timeline (4-week pilot with 2-week prep), success criteria and next steps to exchange security docs and run benchmarks.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-03-15 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), David Patel (Redwood SE), Olivia Torres (Rivermark CISO), Marcus Lee (Infra Lead), Priya Shah (Product)

[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): hey everyone thanks for jumping on, uh appreciate you all making time. quick roll call?
[00:08] Olivia (Rivermark CISO): Olivia here, hi.
[00:09] Marcus (Infra): Marcus here.
[00:13] Priya (Product): Priya on from product.
[00:16] David (Redwood SE): David here, thanks.
[00:20] Maya: cool, goal for today is to scope the security pilot: what Rivermark needs from SOC 2/ISO, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, and then map those to workload sizing and benchmark requirements for the POC. want to align on success criteria and timelines. any additions?
[00:34] Olivia: sounds right. primary lens is compliance — our audit team needs to see attestations and we need to validate data flows for PHI handling.
[00:42] Marcus: and from infra, network and encryption, plus whether we do hosted dedicated or private in our VPC.
[00:49] Priya: product wants to validate latencies for the chat assistant and bulk embedding jobs, and make sure RBAC maps to our roles.
[00:58] Maya: great. quick overview: Redwood offers hosted API, Dedicated reserved pools, and Private VPC/on-prem options. for pilots we typically recommend either a hosted dedicated pool with VPC peering or a private deployment if they require air-gap. we have SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 attestation; i'll share the certs.
[01:18] Olivia: can you send the report, not just cert? auditor wants the attestation and scope.
[01:23] Maya: yes, i'll send SOC 2 Type II attestation plus ISO scope doc.
[01:27] David: and on the technical side i'll include our network diagram, KMS integration notes (we support customer-managed KMS/HSM), and how we handle KV cache and prefix caching — sorry kv cash, transcription — for clarity.
[01:44] Marcus: ok good. for encryption at rest we need AES-256 with CMKs in our KMS and HSM-backed keys for certain datasets. is that supported?
[01:52] David: we support CMK wrapping and HSM-backed keys for private deployments; hosted customers can use Redwood-managed KMS or bring-your-own-key with supported cloud KMS providers. we'll detail that in the pack.
[02:05] Priya: on RBAC, we need role separation: product users, devs, compliance auditors with read-only, and ops with ability to kick off model rollouts. can RBAC integrate with SAML groups?
[02:15] Maya: yes SSO/SAML via Okta works; we map groups to RBAC roles and can enforce least privilege. we'll send an example mapping.
[02:24] Olivia: audit logging — retention requirements: we need 2 years of immutable audit logs for certain actions, and logs should include user, action, timestamp, and request ids. is that feasible?
[02:35] David: yes, we capture request-level audit trails: token usage, model/route, user id, and we can stream logs to your SIEM or to a locked bucket. retention and immutability depend on plan — for private/dedicated we can meet 2-year retention. for hosted we have add-on packages.
[02:53] Marcus: network topology question: can you do VPC peering or do you require a public egress for token traffic?
[02:59] David: we support VPC peering and private link options; for the pilot we can do VPC peering to the dedicated pool or set up a private deployment in your cluster. depends on timing and infra access.
[03:12] Maya: let's talk success criteria and benchmarks — what does Rivermark need to validate in the 4-week pilot?
[03:19] Priya: product wants two things: 1) chat latency within 95th percentile under production-like load — target <200ms for short completions (~50-100 tokens) and <400ms for longer multi-turns; 2) embeddings throughput and cost per embedding under realistic batch sizes.
[03:36] Marcus: infra wants throughput targets: baseline 50 requests per second for the chat route, spike to 200 rps for short windows. need to see how autoscaling and batching behave. also memory and GPU utilization metrics.
[03:50] David: good, i'll prepare a benchmark checklist: synthetic load script, sample payloads (including token sizes), and metrics collection (p95 latency, p99 latency, tokens/sec, GPU utilization). we'll also recommend quantization profiles for cost tests.
[04:05] Olivia: compliance success criteria: receipt of attestations, verification of SSO integration, RBAC mapping tested with at least one auditor account, and audit logs delivered to our SIEM. also a data handling review showing PHI is not persisted beyond configured retention.
[04:21] Maya: agreed. i'd propose pilot scope: 2-week setup (network, SSO, keys, dataset access), 2-week active benchmark and validation. total 4 weeks. during setup David will run initial end-to-end test, then we run scaled benchmarks. acceptable?
[04:37] Marcus: timeline looks ok, but need exact maintenance windows — we prefer weekends for network changes.
[04:42] Maya: noted, will propose dates.
[04:45] Priya: what about data minimization and redaction? we need deterministic PII redaction before logs are sent out.
[04:53] David: we have configurable redaction hooks and can strip or hash PII before persisting. for deeper needs, we can run a preprocessing step in your VPC.
[05:03] Olivia: any pen test / vulnerability scan reports? external pentest?
[05:08] Maya: we have a recent pen test summary; i'll include the executive summary and the remediation timeline. full reports are available under NDA — i'll note that in the pack.
[05:18] Marcus: for benchmarks, what tooling do you recommend? Locust? JMeter? k6?
[05:23] David: we typically provide a k6 script and a python/asyncio load harness that hits the streaming endpoints and non-streaming endpoints. we'll share that and you can run from your load generator or we can run from Redwood side in the dedicated pool.
[05:36] Priya: are you able to run embedding batches of 10k vectors to validate throughput/cost?
[05:41] David: yes, for embedding cost tests we recommend a batch runner and profiling across quantization settings. if you'd like we can run a couple sample runs and share numbers.
[05:51] Maya: any blockers on compliance signoff? Olivia?
[05:54] Olivia: main asks are: full attestation, ability to route audit logs to our SIEM, SSO integration test, and HSM-based key control for PHI. if those are met pilot can proceed.
[06:06] Maya: good — recap of immediate deliverables: security pack (SOC2/ISO + pen test summary), network diagram and KMS options (David), benchmark scripts and checklist (David), sample workload profile (Marcus).
[06:18] Marcus: i'll share the workload profile and a small redacted dataset by Monday.
[06:22] Maya: perfect. any last questions?
[06:24] Priya: just confirming success signal: p95 chat <200ms, embedding throughput X tokens/s TBD after we see dataset, and RBAC + audit logs validated by your compliance team.
[06:35] Maya: yep we'll codify those in the SOW for the pilot. ok thanks everyone, we'll send the pack and proposed dates.
[06:41] Olivia: thanks all.
[06:42] Marcus: thanks.
[06:43] David: thanks, bye.

Notes: Transcript has light ASR errors (KV cash, transcription artifacts). Referenced artifacts: Security Pack (SOC2/ISO/pen-test) - link to be shared, Network diagram (Redwood dedicated/private), Benchmark scripts (k6/python harness), Workload profile (Rivermark sample).
